title: tenant-session-split-causing-imbalance-in-aggregate-billing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers (Dedicated and Private tenants) reported that their invoice line items showed a persistent ~2-4% undercount for the previous billing hour after regional failovers and autoscaler evictions. Investigation indicates the ledger aggregation job is double-counting split session fragments as separate sessions rather than stitching them, which leads to some tokens being attributed to a short-lived ephemeral session that is never reconciled with the canonical tenant session. Impact window varies (typically minutes) and manifests as either under- or over-billing depending on backfill timing.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate a tenant traffic spike on a Dedicated node and trigger an autoscaler eviction (node termination) while streaming responses are active.

Force a proxy-level reconnect for the tenant (simulate TCP reconnect and header rebind) so a new session is created with a new session_id while KV-cache rehydration for the old session is still in-flight.
Emit a sequence of streaming tokens with a short-lived prefetch on the old session, then continue generation on the new session.
Run ledger-rollup for the hour boundary and inspect token attribution for tenant ledgers in the billing dashboard (agg by session_id and by tenant_id).
observations: Two fragments (old_session_x and new_session_y) both have non-zero token counts within the same hour window for the same tenant_id.
Ledger-rollup currently groups by session_id first, then tenant_id, which prevents coalescing of fragments generated within 60s of each other when handoff happens.
KV-prefetch writes can be replayed during reconnects which leaves small token counts on the old session that are never merged.
Affected customers are primarily on Dedicated pools with aggressive autoscaling and some Private clusters that had proxy reconnect patterns during recent maintenance windows.
root_cause_summary: A race between proxy handoff and hourly ledger-rollup: when a tenant session is torn down and re-established rapidly, the system assigns a new session_id but leaves behind small prefetched token artifacts tied to the old session. The ledger aggregation pipeline treats those fragments as separate sessions, causing split attribution. Because downstream billing aggregation prefers session-first grouping, the fragments are sometimes excluded from the tenant's canonical cumulative row during certain window boundary conditions, producing apparent undercounts.
impact_analysis: Number of affected tenants observed so far: 6 (2 enterprise Dedicated, 4 Private trials).
Typical delta per tenant: 0.5%–4% of hourly token usage, concentrated in high-throughput streaming routes.
Financial exposure: estimated $1.8k across escalated tenants in the current month (subject to reconciliation).
Operational risk: potential for customer churn if not resolved and compensated quickly.
mitigation: Hotfix (deployed 2026-02-24 - patch v1): adjust ledger-rollup to: 1) coalesce session fragments that share tenant_id and have session_end/start within a configurable 120s handoff window; 2) canonicalize prefetch writes to attribute to the most recent session where a session continuation header exists. Temporary mitigation also included increasing backfill delay to 3m for suspicious fragment groups to allow coalescing before finalizing hourly rollups.
timeline: 2026-02-18: Customer A opened support ticket describing missing tokens after autoscale eviction.
2026-02-20: Pager rotation alerted SREs to similar anomaly; initial triage tied to reconnect pattern.
2026-02-22: Reproduced locally with test harness that simulates proxy rebind + KV prefetch replay.
2026-02-24: Hotfix deployed to ledger-rollup and ingest-preprocessor; temporary backfill delay enabled.
2026-03-01: Additional reconciliation job run; credits issued to two customers pending legal approval.
2026-03-10: Follow-up validation shows <0.1% residual variance in rerun tests; monitoring rules updated.
resolution_summary: Hotfix implemented to coalesce closely timed session fragments and canonicalize prefetch attribution. Immediate backfill reconciliation ran for escalated tenants; credits issued where delta exceeded SLA thresholds. Monitoring alerts added to detect similar session-split patterns and a dashboard to track fragment coalescing efficacy.
postmortem_actions: BACKLOG-1: Replace session-first grouping in final billing aggregation with tenant-first canonicalization logic (ENG-802400).
BACKLOG-2: Add end-to-end test in chaos harness that simulates node eviction + proxy rebind to prevent regressions.
BACKLOG-3: Update onboarding docs for Dedicated customers to call out recommended autoscaler drain settings.
BACKLOG-4: Automate credit threshold detection and safe-rollback for backfill runs.
customer_communication: 2026-02-25: Sent initial status update to affected customers with temporary mitigation and ETA for fix.
2026-03-02: Sent reconciliation summary and proposed credits for review.
2026-03-05: Legal approved credits; finance applied adjustments to March invoices.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: prefer coalescing in aggregation layer rather than changing client/session contract; lower risk and faster rollout.
Tradeoff: increasing backfill delay adds small latency to finalizing hourly billing snapshots (configurable, default 3m).
Follow-up: instrument more granular session lineage headers in proxy layer so fragments can be deterministically rejoined in the future.
next_steps: Deploy tenant-first canonicalization in release runtime-1.25 (ENG-802400) and run rolling reconciliation on last 90 days for high-value tenants.
Add unit+integration tests to ingest preprocessor that assert idempotent prefetch attribution.
Complete postmortem doc and share with Customer Success and Legal for playbook updates.
